output.source_comparison: Both refer to official Federal Reserve information. Kalshi uses the upper bound published on the Fed's website. Polymarket names the December FOMC statement as its resolution source and also identifies the Fed's website as a source for the level and change. Neither supplied rule establishes a broader source fallback hierarchy.
output.deadline_comparison: Kalshi expires at the first 2:05 PM ET following the meeting statement or one week after the meeting's last day. Polymarket may resolve when the statement with relevant data is issued; if no statement is released by the end date of the next scheduled meeting, it resolves to the No change bracket. The listed close and settlement timestamps differ and do not by themselves establish identical observation windows.
output.boundary_comparison: Kalshi YES requires an upper bound strictly greater than 3.25%; exactly 3.25% is not YES. Polymarket YES concerns a 25-basis-point decrease relative to the pre-meeting level, with unlisted changes rounded up to the nearest 25 basis points; the supplied text does not fully specify every rounding boundary.
differences: Kalshi tests an absolute post-meeting rate; Polymarket tests the size and direction of the change from the pre-meeting rate.
For example, a decrease from 3.50% to 3.25% would be Polymarket YES but Kalshi NO.
Polymarket specifies a no-statement fallback to No change; Kalshi specifies a one-week expiration but does not state the resulting payout in that circumstance.
Kalshi specifies 2:05 PM Eastern Time; Polymarket's rule does not specify a timezone for the next-meeting end-date fallback.
Neither supplied rule specifies cancellation, tie, or 50/50 payout treatment.
output.explanation: The YES conditions have a known material mismatch and are not exact complements. Missing cancellation and exceptional-outcome rules add uncertainty, but do not change the classification of different.
